Finite sample properties cannot be directly equated with asymptotic probability limits which concern the behavior as sample size approaches infinity. The limit matrix Q can be positive semi-definite with zero eigenvalues, invalidating its invertibility. Dividing by n is appropriate, whereas dividing by sqrt(n) causes asymptotic explosion. The probability limit of a matrix does not equal its expected value; the latter is not normalized for sample size. The limit of an inverse matrix is not equivalent to the inverse of the limit.

        sign = 1

        vbb_r, vtt_r, rho_r = rng.randint(20, 40), rng.randint(10, 20), rng.randint(25, 65)
        sign = 1
    elif arch == 3:

        vbb_r, vtt_r, rho_r = rng.randint(12, 30), rng.randint(6, 16), rng.randint(15, 50)
